concepts.name: Chirality & Chiral Center
concepts.definition: Chiral object is non-superimposable on its mirror image (like hands). In molecules, chirality most commonly arises from sp³ carbon with 4 different substituents — a stereocenter. Presence of a chiral center ≠ chiral molecule (meso case cancels).
criteria: No internal plane of symmetry in whole molecule
Tetrahedral geometry allows two 3-D arrangements that are mirror images

examples.name: 2-Butanol
examples.stereocenter: C-2 has OH, CH3, H, C2H5 → chiral

identificationSteps: Find each sp³ carbon; list its 4 attachments up to symmetry (consider entire substituent, not just first atom)
Count stereocenters: n centers → up to 2ⁿ stereoisomers (fewer if meso)

concepts.name: R/S Absolute Configuration (Cahn-Ingold-Prelog, CIP)
concepts.definition: R (rectus, clockwise) / S (sinister, counterclockwise) assigns absolute 3-D arrangement at each stereocenter using CIP priority rules based on atomic number.
rules: 1. Rank the 4 substituents by atomic number (Z) of atom directly bonded to stereocenter. Higher Z = higher priority (I > Br > Cl > S > F > O > N > C > H; lone pair = 0).

2. If tie, move outward atom-by-atom along substituent; at first point of difference, higher Z wins. Double/triple bonds treated as duplicated single bonds: C=O → C bonded to O,O,C; C≡C → C bonded to C,C,C.
3. Place lowest priority (4) to the back (dash, going away). If it is wedged forward, swap any two groups to put it back and invert final answer.
4. Trace 1→2→3 ignoring 4: clockwise = R, counterclockwise = S.

examples.assignment: With H to back, OH→COOH→CH3 trace; example arrangement gives S (if trace counterclockwise). Mirror image = R.
examples.tip: In Fischer, horizontal = wedge (forward), vertical = dash (back).

examples.assignment: Simple atomic number series → easy trace.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to put lowest priority to back before tracing; if 4 is on wedge, answer inverts.
Treating -CH(CH3)2 vs -CH2CH2CH3: need to go to second sphere; branching matters.
Double bond duplication: -CHO (C bonded to O,O,H) outranks -CH2OH (C bonded to O,H,H).

concepts.name: E/Z Alkene Isomerism (CIP for double bonds)
concepts.definition: E (entgegen, opposite) / Z (zusammen, together) describes relative positions of high-priority groups on each sp² carbon of a C=C. Replaces unreliable cis/trans when more than 2 different substituents.
rules: For each sp² carbon of C=C separately, rank its two substituents by CIP (same rules as R/S).
Determine where the #1 priority on carbon-1 sits relative to #1 on carbon-2 across the double bond.
If both #1 priorities are on SAME side → Z (zusammen); if OPPOSITE sides → E (entgegen).

examples.Z: Both CH3 on same side = (Z)-2-butene (cis, Z)

examples.assignment: If Br and F same side → Z; opposite → E. Note cis/trans would be ambiguous because 4 different groups.

concepts.cisTransVsEZ: cis/trans only meaningful when each C has one H (or clearly 'same groups'). For highly substituted alkenes (3-4 carbons), always use E/Z via CIP.

concepts.name: Enantiomers, Diastereomers, Meso & Racemic Mixtures

relationships.definition: Pair of stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images. Identical physical properties (mp, bp, IR, NMR) except optical rotation [α]D opposite sign (± equal magnitude) and interaction with other chiral environments (enzymes, chiral reagents).
relationships.example: (R)-lactic acid [α] = -3.8° vs (S)-lactic acid [α] = +3.8°; NMR identical in achiral solvent.
relationships.test: Racemic mixture (± 1:1) is optically inactive; meso not formed.

relationships.definition: Stereoisomers that are NOT mirror images. Different physical and chemical properties (mp, bp, Rf, NMR δ different).
relationships.example: (2R,3R)-tartaric acid vs (2R,3S)-tartaric acid (meso). Also E vs Z alkenes are diastereomers; cis vs trans cycloalkanes.
relationships.energy: Diastereomers have different stability; may be separable by standard chromatography.

relationships.definition: Has stereocenters but is achiral due to internal plane of symmetry; non-superimposable mirror is identical via rotation. Despite 2 stereocenters, only 3 stereoisomers not 4.
relationships.example: (2R,3S)-tartaric acid HOOC-C*H(OH)-C*H(OH)-COOH: the two centers are opposite (R,S) → internal plane between C2-C3 cancels chirality; optically inactive, meso. Also meso-2,3-butanediol.
relationships.recognition: Draw Fischer with vertical carbon chain; if top half mirrors bottom half (plane through middle), meso.

relationships.definition: 1:1 equimolar mixture of two enantiomers. Optically inactive (rotations cancel). Physical properties similar to pure enantiomer but may differ in mp/crystal form (racemic vs conglomerate).
relationships.separation: Resolved via chiral resolving agent (diastereomeric salt formation, e.g., racemic acid + chiral amine → salts with different solubility) or chiral chromatography.

relationships.definition: Diastereomers differing at exactly ONE stereocenter (among ≥2).
relationships.example: D-glucose vs D-mannose (epimer at C-2); D-glucose vs D-galactose (C-4).

relationships.definition: Epimers at the anomeric carbon (hemiacetal carbon) of cyclic sugars. α-anomer: OH trans to CH2OH (axial in glucose); β-anomer: OH cis (equatorial). Mutarotation interconverts via open chain.

concepts.maxIsomers: For molecule with n stereocenters: max 2ⁿ stereoisomers. Subtract meso duplicates. E.g., 2 centers → 4 combos (RR, SS enantiomers; RS, SR enantiomers) but if RS = SR identical (meso) → 3 total.

concepts.name: Conformation, Fischer, Newman & Chair

conformation.detail: Staggered (60° dihedral, low energy) vs eclipsed (0°, high due to torsional strain). Barrier ~12 kJ/mol. Anti (180°) most stable in butane.
conformation.diagram: Newman: front carbon dot, back circle; 3 lines each.

conformation.detail: Most stable: all angles 109.5°, staggered, no angle/torsional strain. Chair interconversion (ring flip) swaps axial ↔ equatorial. Axial substituents experience 1,3-diaxial interactions (~7 kJ per axial CH3); equatorial more stable. tert-Butyl locks chair equatorially.
conformation.axialEquatorial: Axial: parallel to C3 axis, alternating up/down; Equatorial: roughly in-plane, also alternating but opposite. Cis-1,2-disubstituted: one axial one equatorial (a,e) in both chair forms.

concepts.fischer: Fischer projection: vertical line = dashes (back), horizontal = wedges (forward). Carbon chain vertical, most oxidized C at top (aldehyde for sugars). D/L determined by OH on highest chiral C far from carbonyl: D = OH on right (in Fischer), L = on left (historical glyceraldehyde standard). D/L not related to +/- rotation or R/S.
concepts.opticalRotation: [α]D^T = α / (l·c) where α observed rotation (°), l path length (dm), c concentration (g/mL). Dextrorotatory (+) rotates clockwise viewed toward light; levorotatory (−) counterclockwise. R/S does NOT correlate with +/- (e.g., (R)-lactic acid is levorotatory).
concepts.resolutionMethods: Racemate resolution: 1) Diastereomeric salt (Pasteur), 2) Chiral chromatography, 3) Enzymatic resolution (enantioselective enzyme), 4) Asymmetric synthesis (chiral catalyst → one enantiomer).

quickReference.rsAssignmentMnemonic: CIP → point lowest to back → 1→2→3 clockwise = R (Right), counterclockwise = S (Sinistra). Clockwise R, Counterclockwise S.
quickReference.ezMnemonic: Z = Zusammen (together): high priorities together; E = Entgegen (opposite): high priorities opposite.
quickReference.cisTransLimit: Use cis/trans only for disubstituted alkenes with H or ring; else use E/Z.
quickReference.chiralCenterTest: 4 different groups? → stereocenter. Then check whole molecule for plane of symmetry → if none, chiral.
quickReference.enantiomerProperties: Enantiomers: identical mp/bp/IR/NMR; opposite optical rotation; different biological activity (e.g., (S)-thalidomide teratogenic vs R sedative; (S)-ibuprofen active). Diastereomers differ in all properties.
